title: N-Queens
prompt:
Place `n` queens on an `n×n` board so none attack each other, and return all distinct solutions. Each solution is a list of board rows, where `'Q'` is a queen and `'.'` is empty.

**Example**: `n = 4` → `[[".Q..","...Q","Q...","..Q."],["..Q.","Q...","...Q",".Q.."]]`.

Place one queen per row; track threatened columns and both diagonals with boolean arrays for O(1) safety checks.
hints: Recurse row by row; a queen at (row, col) claims that column, the diagonal `row-col`, and the anti-diagonal `row+col`.
Use boolean arrays `cols`, `diag`, `anti` (offset diagonal indices to stay non-negative).
When you place a queen in the last row, snapshot the board into a list of strings.

solution.explanation: One queen per row removes the row conflict automatically. Cells on the same ↘ diagonal share `row - col`; on the same ↙ anti-diagonal share `row + col` — so three boolean arrays make each safety test O(1). Adding `n` to the diagonal index keeps it non-negative for array use.
